messages:
anya: Heads up - dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-prod-3' started oscillating after the 02:00 deploy, seeing scale up -> scale down -> scale up in ~90s and a burst of 503s for a single tenant. Example logs attached below.

sam: Ugh. Any idea what's triggering it? autoscaler or healthchecks?

anya: autoscaler-bot flagged multiple rapid events: 5 scale events in 2m. stack trace shows scale_down triggered by low queued_requests metric immediately after scale_up succeeded.

ops-bot: [AUTOSCALER] pool=eu-west-2-prod-3 event=scale_up from=2 to=5 reason="latency_sla_breach"; event_ts=2834567891
ops-bot: [AUTOSCALER] pool=eu-west-2-prod-3 event=scale_down from=5 to=2 reason="queued_requests_below_threshold"; event_ts=2834567950

leo: Could be a race: short-lived spike pushes up, then a trailing worker finishes and queued_requests dips below threshold, causing immediate scale down. cooldown might be too low.

anya: Here are snippets from the tenant's error stream:
```
2026-06-12T02:01:12Z tenant=brightcart req_id=abc123 status=200 rt=120ms
2026-06-12T02:01:34Z tenant=brightcart req_id=def456 status=503 rt=0ms backend_err="no_worker_available"
2026-06-12T02:01:54Z tenant=brightcart req_id=ghi789 status=200 rt=95ms
```

sam: The 503s line up with the window between scale_down and new worker warmup. Were we applying prefix cache warmups?

anya: Not for this tenant - they hit a cold path. Also noticed a flurry of KV eviction logs around the same time. memory pressure on a subset of pods.

infra-bot: [METRICS] pool=eu-west-2-prod-3 memory_p99=87% -> 96% at 02:00; kv_evictions increased by 400/s; heartbeat_misses=3 in 60s

leo: Heartbeat_misses might be a red herring. Are heartbeats used in the autoscaler decision? I thought we only used queue length & latency percentiles.

anya: Config shows: autoscaler uses latency_p95, queued_requests, and node_health (heartbeat). Node_health is weighted low but heartbeat_misses currently set to immediately mark candidate for scale down. That's too aggressive.

oncall-raja: I'm oncall - I've run a repro in staging by replaying a small spike and then immediate drop; autoscaler does the same. Repro steps: 1) send 200 concurrent short requests; 2) stop load; 3) observe scale_up then scale_down in ~45-70s.

sam: Good repro. Quick mitigation: increase scale_down cooldown from 60s to 180s and add a 30s moving-average on queued_requests to avoid reacting to single-worker completions. Can we patch and rollout a 10% config change to eu-west-2?

leo: Also add a small hysteresis so we require queued_requests < threshold for 2 consecutive samples. That prevents flipflop.

anya: Will open a config change PR. In parallel, is there customer impact to communicate? Brightcart saw ~30 failed calls (500/503) for ~2m window. Billing/SLAs?

sam: Notify CS@brightcart and log incident. Not major but callouts needed. Add an opt-in setting in Dedicated to increase cooldown by default for bursty tenants?

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-6459 linked to thread.

anya: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/autoscaler/changes/689 - patch increases cooldown and adds two-sample hysteresis. Rolling to eu-west-2-prod-3 as canary now.

oncall-raja: Canary applied. Monitoring dashboards show scale events suppressed in next 10m. Will keep watch; if stable, promote to all clusters.

sam: Followups: 1) investigate KV eviction spike root cause (maybe noisy neighbor tenant uploads), 2) consider warm pool option for heavy prefixes, 3) test different cooldowns under synthetic workloads.

leo: Re noisy neighbor - we saw one tenant doing periodic batch jobs without tenant isolation limiting cache pressure. Let's file a task to throttle background jobs or apply tenancy QoS.

anya: Filing follow-ups and will update INC-2026-6459. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: [AUTOSCALER] canary=eu-west-2-prod-3 config=canary-689 status=healthy - no new scale_down within 5m

sam: Great. Postmortem draft please if we see recurrence.

anya: Will write a short postmortem in /docs/incidents once we verify stability.
